title: LIT as taught, NY killzones, market entry
question: Does the owner's LIT method (Liquidity Inducement Theorem) beat the Liquidity Engine?
verdict: Pure LIT (sweep -> structure shift, market entry next bar, stop beyond the protected low) in the NY killzones: too few trades (0.5/wk in 2026) and it loses money in 2021-25.
notes: engine/lit.py + tools/research_lit.py; separate strategy, not the live engine; no cold-streak filter; size $800 up to a 20-pt stop then 800x20/stop, MNQ, max 40 micros, $1.40/micro + 1 tick slippage
method: LIT replay (engine/lit.py run_x, the same code as the live loop engine/lit_live.py): 2026 entries on 1-minute bars, 2021-25 on 5-minute bars (reference); live sizing + weekly stop; costs included
